Name: Case Study
Description: An in-depth investigation of a particular case or event. Often seen in the medical field when examining a specific patient or illness, but can also be seen within law and political fields. Tries to take an isolated incident and generate a more generalizable theory that still needs to be tested.

Name: Survey
Description: An extraction of data from a particular group of interest. Can be conducted through online communication methods or in-person. Often used to find data such as demographics, opinions and feelings, or other information for social research purposes.

Name: Ethnography
Description: Documentation of a particular setting or people in order to find patterns in social interaction or perception. As a study of cultures, it can be applied to a wide range of different target groups. Focuses on qualitative data, such as observation notes and experiences, interviews, and more.

Name: Focus Group
Description: A group interview with preset demographics involving a small number of participants . Tries to focus on reactions and opinions to researcher questions. Works to find group reactions and experiences as feedback to researchers.

Name: Content Analysis
Description: A study of archival documents and communicative artifacts. Examination ideally leads to identifying patterns in communication through replicable examples. This can be seen through qualitative analysis, such as examining page area in a journal or newspaper, but can also be seen as quantitative analysis, such as word frequencies or quantifying lengths of commercials on television.

Name: Digital Trace Research
Description: Uses passively generated data, such as cellphone activity or web searches, to analyze human behavior and communication. Uses raw data that avoids skewing from the participant. Allows the examination of complex social networks and enables trends to be identified for large concepts.

Name: Randomized Control Trials
Description: An experimental method designed to increase levels of control to find viable data. Minimizes bias through the randomization of groups and treatments. Found in clinical trials when applying new medicinal methods to find unbiased data of treatment efficacy.

Name: Quasi-Experimental Study
Description: An experimental examination that uses predetermined or not randomly selected groups. Similar to experimental procedures, attempts to identify causal relationships. However, confounding variables possibly exist within the experiment, so data may be influenced.

Name: Correlational Study
Description: A statistical analysis between two or more variables. Attempts to identify if two or more things have a significant relationship with each other. Does not identify the cause of the relationship between both variables, only identifies if there is a possible relationship.

Name: Longitudinal Study
Description: A study that is spread over a long period of time. It follows the same participants and includes variables and measures long-term relationships that may appear long after short term data is collected. Can study relationships for a lifetime or even generations to identify patterns.

Name: Policy Research
Description: Identifies how policies influence populations. Can be interactions with previously created legislature or the examination of processes with current policy. Results and feedback from this research allow for improvements to future policies that are drafted and implemented.

Name: Systematic Reviews
Description: A synthesis of a clear topic that takes many different arguments and creates an evidence based conclusion. For example, can take multiple different clinical trials and identify general trends in treating an illness from multiple different studies. Often reviews the quantitative results and mixed method evidence presented to draw numerical conclusions.
